label: Early-to-mid original-phase first occurrence of b/d/h/r/i/o/p/m, gated by first token (1,t,w,c,n,z,y,v)
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, almost entirely at t=2..6 (peak t=3-4); never at t=0, the delimiter, or the copy phase. It needs a specific current input: b is by far the strongest (9x lift, 35% of mass, and every top activation is b), then d, h, r, and more weakly i, o, p, m. Digits and most other letters rarely trigger it. It almost always fires on the first occurrence of that token (94% of mass). Whether it fires also depends heavily on sequence context: rates are much higher when the sequence starts with 1, t, w, c, n, z, y or v (top examples look like 1 1 y e [b]), and the prev2_tok table shows a similar preference for these tokens, which suggests it is reading a hidden-state context built from earlier tokens. The predicate conjoins token set, position window, first occurrence and first-token set: dev F1 0.42, precision 0.31, recall 0.63, mass recall 0.71. Many b/d/h/r first occurrences in favourable contexts still do not fire, so the context dependence is only approximated.
